missing_ops.name: fixed_point_quantize

missing_ops.name: hash / merkle_commit / vector_commit
missing_ops.what: no operator computes a digest of a state dict, a Merkle root or a Pedersen/KZG commitment, so c_D, c_u, h_t, h_Pi and the optimizer-state commitments cannot be produced or checked

missing_ops.name: range_proof / interval_membership

missing_ops.name: verify_proof / fold_proofs
missing_ops.what: no proof-system operator of any kind; this is also the cryptographic protocol that rule 3 keeps out of plugins, so it is listed for completeness of the cost measurement, not as a request

extraction_needs.via: train_trace/TraceView gives per-step scalars recorded after the fact, not the sampler's inputs; no hook or operator re-derives or vetoes a batch, so third-party replay (steps 4-5) has nothing to attach to

extraction_needs.where: client, before and after each optimizer step (CLIENT_PRE_STEP / CLIENT_STEP)
extraction_needs.via: GradientView exposes gradients and parameter values only; no optimizer-state kind exists; eta appears only as the 'lr' scalar handed to on_step after the step (TraceView.series('lr'))

extraction_needs.data: the activations, per-token logits and per-token loss the circuit arithmetizes
extraction_needs.via: LossView gives batch, outputs, loss, per_sample_losses(), gradients_of() (one backward each) and loss_on(); deeper quantities cost ModelHandle passes (hidden/activations/per_sample_gradients) and the client handle may be absent

extraction_needs.data: the leaf/epoch/final proofs travelling from client to aggregator, and the verdict they yield

deviations: The cryptographic protocol is not ported (rule 3): no commitments, no field arithmetic, no proofs, no recursion; the verdicts arrive as the `vft_verdicts` resource, so what the plugins contain is VFT's decision rule, not VFT's verification.
Step 6 is counted as ported for its enforcement half only: the boolean quota check becomes a mask_samples drop; the quota certificate (commitment to e_t, range proof on gamma) is not implemented.
rounds_per_epoch replaces the epoch boundary the library does not expose; the paper's own epoch accounting is inconsistent (one epoch vs 'every 10th epoch is public').

Bins come from SampleRecord.source (the paper's domain attribute) by default; register/length/policy buckets need a defender-supplied bin_of, and the token ceilings of Table IV are out of reach because only character lengths are visible.
Over-quota samples are dropped, not replaced: no action can ask the host for a different batch, whereas VFT draws the batch from (s, t) (public mode) or inside the circuit (private mode).
Admission is charged per distinct sample hash and masking is by hash, so identical texts in one round are admitted or dropped together.
VFT's quota violation aborts aggregation; the library has no abort action, so the round is aborted by excluding every participant (in the harness the previous global model is then left in place).
A participant without a passing verdict is excluded by default, since VFT accepts only verified updates; on_missing='flag' is offered for deployments that want the gate as a monitor.

Taint persists in ctx.state until a verdict of 'ok' arrives, i.e. until the verifier attests a corrected manifest; a tainted client is removed from aggregation but is not stopped from training locally.
The client's bin counters travel as an ordinary untrusted message; VFT's local quota commitment is a proof object the library cannot carry, so the counters are readable but unbound.
The plugin proposes no weights: VFT does not reweight updates, and the risk score it reports is a boolean mapped to 0.0/1.0 for the recorder.
open_choices: Default binning by the source tag alone; the paper's length and register buckets need edges it does not give.
Admission inside a bin's remaining budget is a uniform draw from ctx.rng taken in sorted bin order; the paper's public mode uses a CSPRNG seeded by (s, t).
rounds_per_epoch = 1 by default as the epoch-to-round mapping.
A bin absent from `quota` is unbounded (default_limit = inf), because the paper never says what an unlisted bin means.
The verdict vocabulary (ok / tainted / quota_violation) and the missing-verdict default are this plugin's construction, since the paper states outcomes rather than a status format.
Excluding every participant is the expression of 'abort the round', and exclusion is scoped to aggregation only.
The sizes of the thin local-proof subset and of the aggregator's random check are left to the verifier, as the paper does not give them.
The 0.0/1.0 participant score is an invention for the record, not a paper quantity.
needs_from_authors: PROVEUPDATE pseudocode, announced in Sec. III.K but absent from the extracted text: without it the witness layout and constraint arrangement of a step proof cannot be defined, so no step-proof interface can be built.

The concrete softmax/GELU/rsqrt approximations (polynomial or rational form, clipping range, lookup table sizes, interpolation) and the numeric epsilon_fxp, tau and GELU budget; tau = delta_sm + epsilon_fxp cannot be instantiated from the paper.
Merkle tree arity and hash instantiation, plus the Pedersen/KZG parameters and SRS size.

How the binning matrix M combines domain, register and length into B rows and whether Eq. (3) is per attribute or joint; how Table IV's ceilings convert to batch size 64 and steps per epoch; how global quotas and fairness counters combine with local ones.

The size of the thin subset of steps a client proves, the size of the random subset the aggregator checks, and the test statistic and threshold of the probabilistic audit (only detection probabilities are reported).

Whether the proven fixed-point shadow computation is the released model or a parallel witness, and the recovery semantics after a tainted client is excluded (full re-aggregation vs rolling back its contribution).
The VFT-FrontEnd/SamplerGuard implementation, to see what per-step data the prover actually consumes.
report.confidence_reason: The library-side facts (stages, kinds, actions, view methods, the 65536-byte message cap, the absence of any optimizer-state or proof operator) are read straight off the reference, and the two ported decision points are tested end to end on synthetic LoRA state dicts. What keeps this from high confidence is the paper side: PROVEUPDATE is missing, the binning and quota-to-runtime mapping is unspecified, and the paper's epoch accounting contradicts itself, so the plugin shapes here are my construction around two decisions whose verdicts are computed outside the library. One library fact was learned the hard way and is now respected by the test: the runner turns `proposals` into `actions` records and empties the field, so the mask is asserted through its applied effect (`kept_indices`/`training_samples`/`training_hashes`) and the client's report through `outbox()`, not through `findings.proposals` or the raw message keys. This environment has no fedguard checkout and is read-only, so the plugin logic was traced against the reference and the harness rather than re-run here.
